article.headline: ConocoPhillips Grows Earnings 107% As Oil Holds Above $100
article.deck: The oil producer is 1.2% above the 135.97 buy point of a 21-week cup and inside a buy range that runs to 142.77.
body: ConocoPhillips pumps oil and gas on several continents. It finds, produces, moves and sells crude oil, bitumen, natural gas, liquefied natural gas and natural gas liquids, and reports in five segments: Alaska, the Lower 48, Canada, Europe, Middle East and North Africa, and Asia Pacific. Its holdings run from North American shale and Canadian oil sands to conventional fields in Europe, Asia and Australia and global LNG projects.

The quarters show why the stock has worked. Earnings rose 107.1% to $3.23 a share in the June quarter, on revenue up 36.8% to $19.16 billion. That followed $1.38, $1.17 and $1.78 a share in the three quarters before. Revenue went from $15.03 billion to $13.39 billion, then $15.76 billion and $19.16 billion. The next report is due Nov. 5.

The market is not paying much for that growth. ConocoPhillips is valued at $165.3 billion and trades at 13.7 times forward earnings and 18.2 times trailing earnings. The stock is up 47.0% this year and 49.6% over the past year.

The chart is a 21-week cup that ran 24.4% deep, from a March 30 high to a July 1 low of 102.69. The stock cleared the 135.97 buy point Sept. 1, on volume 0.94 times its 50-day average, short of the heavy volume a strong breakout carries. On Monday it rose 3.46, or 2.6%, to 137.56, 1.2% above the buy point, though volume ran only 0.66 times average. The buy range runs to 142.77.

Twenty-eight sessions after the breakout, the stock is still in range, 2.9% below its 52-week high of 141.62. It holds above its 21-day line at 130.73 and its 50-day line at 129.72. ConocoPhillips carries an RS rank of 86 of 99 on the desk's list and leads the energy group, but its RS line is 16.1% below its high.

The headlines are about oil and a deal. A Saturday headline said the stock rose 5.8% after analyst optimism and a $7 billion asset offer, and another said oil is over $100 with that $7 billion offer on the table. A Monday piece pointed to a ramping free cash flow profile. After hours the stock was unchanged at 137.56.
article.watch: A close above the 141.62 high on rising volume, or the Nov. 5 earnings report.

article.deck: GitLab cleared a 55.65 buy point from a five-week cup on Monday and sits in the buy range up to 58.43, but volume ran below average.
body: GitLab rose 0.92, or 1.7%, to 56.01, closing 0.6% above the 55.65 buy point of a five-week cup. The base ran 20.4% deep from its Sept. 2 high to a Sept. 28 low of 44.22. The buy range runs to 58.43. Volume came in at 0.86 times the 50-day average, light for a breakout day.

The stock closed 1.1% below its 52-week high of 56.64. It trades well above its 21-day line at 50.17 and its 50-day line at 45.86, which it leads by 22.1%. GitLab holds an RS rank of 94 of 99 on the desk's list, though its RS line is 3.7% below its own high. Shares are up 49.2% this year and 69.8% over three months.

The fundamentals are about sales, not profits. In the quarter ended July 31 GitLab lost 22 cents a share, its fourth straight loss in the table, after losses of 5 cents, 2 cents and 3 cents. Revenue rose 21.3% to $286.3 million, and it has climbed every quarter shown, from $244.4 million. The next report is due Dec. 1. The company is valued at $9.3 billion and trades at 53.9 times forward earnings.

GitLab announced the foundation for what it calls the Governed Software Factory on Oct. 6. A Sept. 20 headline reported that the chief financial officer's stake dropped by more than 30,000 shares, worth $1.6 million, after the stock hit a 52-week high. After hours the stock was unchanged at 56.01.
A close back under 55.65 would turn this into a stalled breakout; a push to new highs on heavier volume would fix the light-volume flaw.
article.watch: Whether volume picks up as GitLab tests its 56.64 high, and whether it holds 55.65.

fundamentals.summary: Chevron Corporation, through its subsidiaries, engages in the integrated energy and chemicals operations. It operates through Upstream and Downstream segments. The Upstream segment engages in the exploration for, development, production, and transportation of crude oil and natural gas; processing, liquefaction, transportation, and regasification of liquefied natural gas; transportation of crude oil through pipelines; transportation, storage, and marketing of natural gas; carbon capture and storage; and operation of a gas-to-liquids plant. The Downstream segment refines crude oil into petroleum

article.headline: Chevron Rises 1.4% As CEO Calls Fuel Export Decision Unwise
article.deck: Chevron sits 0.1% above the 214.81 buy point of a 23-week cup, inside a buy range up to 225.55, 19 sessions after a breakout that has not run.
body: Chevron gained 3.02, or 1.4%, to 215.00 on volume 0.93 times its 50-day average. The close is 0.1% above the 214.81 buy point of a 23-week cup that ran 23.3% deep from its March 30 high to a July 1 low of 164.78. The stock broke out Sept. 15 on volume 1.22 times average. The buy range runs to 225.55.

Nineteen sessions later, the stock sits right on its buy point, a breakout that has gone nowhere. The close is 1.3% below the 52-week high of 217.78. Chevron trades above its 21-day line at 208.05 and its 50-day line at 204.64. It holds an RS rank of 80 of 99 on the desk's list, but its RS line is 17.1% below its high. Shares are up 41.1% this year.

Earnings rose 321.4% to $6.11 a share in the June quarter, on revenue up 51.4% to $67.2 billion. The three prior quarters earned $1.82, $1.39 and $1.11 a share, on revenue of $48.2 billion, $45.8 billion and $47.6 billion. The next report is due Oct. 30. Chevron is valued at $421.7 billion and trades at 14.6 times forward earnings.

Monday's headlines said Chevron's CEO called a key decision on diesel and fuel exports unwise, and that Chevron and Egypt discussed next steps for the Aphrodite gas pipeline. Another pointed to a CFO shake-up tying new energies to core operations. After hours the stock was unchanged at 215.00.
A move to the 217.78 high would show the breakout has life; a close back under 214.81 would leave it stalled.
article.watch: The 217.78 high and the Oct. 30 report.

market_note: The desk labels the market in correction. The S&P 500 slipped 0.1% to 7807.24 and the Nasdaq fell 0.4% to 27245.9, both still above their 50-day lines by 1.3% and 2.4%, while the Dow rose 0.4% to 51850.55 but sits 1.5% below its 50-day line. Distribution has piled up: seven days on the S&P 500, four on the Nasdaq and six on the Dow over the last 25 sessions, including Oct. 7 and Oct. 8 on the S&P 500. Leadership is thin but not gone: eight names sit on the desk's breakouts-this-week list, software (GitLab, Zeta Global, Palantir) and energy (Chevron, ConocoPhillips) supply most of the names in buy range, and the AI chip group still carries the list's highest average RS rank at 82 even as SanDisk, Arm, Astera Labs, Lam Research and Taiwan Semi sit on the sell-signal list. After hours, the only list name moving 3% or more was Venu Holding, up 3.3% to 1.26, a stock ranked 1 of 99 on the desk's list.
